entry.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
entry.summary: Weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance in language model pretraining, yet a unified understanding of why such control helps and how much is needed remains incomplete. We analyze norm control in Muon over the entire training trajectory using the \emph{accumulated effective learning rate}, $C_T=\sum_{t<T}η_t/\|W_t\|_F$, where $η_t$ is the nominal learning rate and $η_t/\|W_t\|_F$ is the effective learning rate relative to the weight norm. For bounded update directions, accumulation over any training interval bounds relative weight displacement. We show that vanilla Muon can accumulate only logarithmically, potentially limiting exploration and helping explain its slower empirical progress, whereas MuonW and MuonH guarantee at least linear accumulation under the stated conditions. Going beyond bounded-norm control, we show that sufficiently slow norm growth guarantees faster accumulation than the logarithmic worst case, opening up less restrictive optimizer designs. Based on this insight, we propose MuonGS, which uses Gram--Schmidt (GS) projection to remove the radial component of each Muon update without fixing the weight norm. With bounded update directions and a constant nominal learning rate, we prove that the weight norm grows at most proportionally to $\sqrt{t}$ after $t$ steps. Consequently, MuonGS guarantees $C_T=Ω(\sqrt{T})$, with accumulation sustained even in later training. Further, for smooth scale-invariant objectives we establish its $O(T^{-1/2})$ stationarity guarantee. In pretraining experiments with 160M- and 400M-parameter dense models as well as a 135M active- and 1B total- parameter MoE model, MuonGS achieves lower validation perplexity than MuonH at long training horizons. In particular, for the dense model it achieves an estimated token-equivalent speedup up to about $15\%$ at matched validation loss to MuonH.

entry.title: Lower- and upper-$C^2$ integrands: a structured class of functions for stochastic nonconvex optimization
entry.summary: We study nonconvex stochastic functions that admit a structured second-order representation, a generalization of lower- and upper-$C^2$ functions to normal integrands. Similarly to the deterministic case, lower-$C^2$ normal integrands are defined as the pointwise maxima over a compact random index set of functions that are twice-continuously differentiable in the decision variable with an integrable bounded Hessian. Our main result is a local value function characterization of this class of functions, namely, that they satisfy a local sufficient ascent property almost surely. Equivalently, they differ from a convex normal integrand by a random quadratic. The upper-$C^2$ theory follows by a change of sign, and delivers the corresponding lower envelopes, the form in which these integrands appear as second-stage value functions of stochastic programs with compact recourse. We also show that for this class integrability of the function values, of the local Lipschitz moduli, and of the minimum-norm Clarke subgradients are equivalent. We then study smooth integrands, finite lower envelopes, difference-of-convex integrands, Moreau and forward--backward envelopes, compositions with a smooth map, monotone convex compositions, and compact-recourse stochastic programs within these classes of nonconvex stochastic functions. As an application, we show that the optimistic loss of partial-label regression and the variational formulation of the conditional value-at-risk fit within this framework.

entry.title: Linear-quadratic mean field games with Volterra dynamics
entry.summary: We study a class of linear-quadratic mean field games in which the state of each agent follows a stochastic Volterra equation of convolution type. The resulting dynamics are non-Markovian and account for memory effects through a completely monotone kernel, while the mean field interaction enters both the drift and diffusion coefficients. Exploiting a Markovian lifting of the Volterra dynamics, which restores the Markov property at the price of moving to an infinite-dimensional state space, we characterize the optimal response of a representative agent for a given population mean through a system of Riccati equations in Banach spaces, thereby obtaining a feedback representation of the optimal control. We then study the consistency condition defining the mean field equilibrium, which reduces to a forward-backward fixed point equation for the equilibrium mean: we prove existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium on short horizons and, when the control does not act on the diffusion coefficient, on arbitrary horizons under a monotonicity condition on the interaction. Finally, we consider the corresponding finite-player game and establish a quantitative propagation of chaos result. As a consequence, the feedback control of any mean field equilibrium, when implemented by each agent on its own state, yields an $\varepsilon_N$-Nash equilibrium for the $N$-player game, with an explicit rate as the number of agents tends to infinity.

entry.title: GNBG-C: A Unified and Configurable Benchmark Generator for Constrained Continuous Optimization
entry.summary: Many real-world optimization tasks are governed not only by what should be optimized, but also by what is allowed: a solution must first satisfy physical, operational, safety, budgetary, or structural requirements before its objective value becomes meaningful. Yet benchmark design for constrained continuous optimization often treats these restrictions as fixed properties of predefined test instances. Existing generators and benchmark suites provide essential foundations for reproducible comparison, but they either focus primarily on configurable objective landscapes or expose constraint properties within limited, predefined regimes, making it difficult to ask targeted questions about constraint-induced difficulty: whether an optimizer struggles because feasible regions are small, boundaries are restrictive, variables are tightly coupled, or constraint information is poorly scaled. We introduce GNBG-C, a Generalized Numerical Benchmark Generator for Constrained Continuous Optimization. The central idea is to treat the feasible region itself as a configurable object rather than as an inseparable attachment to a fixed test function. By generating controlled constraint regimes around the known GNBG global minimizer, the generator enables systematic studies in which feasibility pressure can be varied while preserving that point as a global minimizer of the constrained problem. This allows researchers to examine how optimizers discover feasibility, handle constraint pressure, and improve objective quality under diverse and controllable feasibility conditions. GNBG-C therefore provides a flexible and auditable framework for probing the strengths and weaknesses of constrained continuous optimizers under targeted forms of feasibility-side difficulty.

entry.title: No closed-form formula for Stiefel geodesics
entry.summary: We use differential Galois theory to prove that given two arbitrary points $X$ and $Y$ on the Stiefel manifold, there is no closed-form analytic expression for the Riemannian logarithm $\log_X Y$, the geodesic between $X$ and $Y$, or the geodesic distance between $X$ and $Y$. In other words, these cannot be expressed in terms of elementary functions of the coordinates of $X$ and $Y$; in fact, our result goes further --- even if we allow for repeated integrals of elementary functions, there is still no such expression.

entry.title: Constructing Data-Driven Budgeted Uncertainty Sets for Robust Optimization
entry.summary: In robust optimization, budgeted uncertainty sets offer a popular trade-off between modeling flexibility and computational tractability. Data that is observed in practice is often discrete in nature, which creates the need for tools to construct budgeted uncertainty sets based on observed data. This paper presents a principled approach for this purpose, which ensures that any solution found through the robust problem with respect to the constructed budgeted uncertainty set offers an approximation guarantee with respect to the optimal value of the problem with discrete data. Our approach is purely based on the geometry of data and can be applied to any nominal optimization problem. We discuss the problem of evaluating budgeted uncertainty sets, and how to construct them using exact and heuristic methods. In computational experiments, we show that it is possible to construct sets with little computation time that offer guarantees that are close to optimality.

entry.title: DREAM: Delay-Resistant Acceleration with Momentum
entry.summary: With exact, delay-free gradients, Nesterov's accelerated gradient (NAG) achieves optimal $\sqrtκ$ dependence for $L$-smooth, $μ$-strongly convex objectives, where $κ=L/μ$; heavy-ball (HB) achieves the same scaling on strongly convex quadratics. In asynchronous and distributed settings, gradients can be inexact, with delays varying across workers and iterations. We isolate staleness using a fixed delay $τ\ge1$, replacing $\nabla f(y_k)$ with $\nabla f(y_{k-τ})$ at iteration $k$. Arjevani, Shamir, and Srebro establish a worst-case lower bound of $Ω(τ\sqrtκ\log(1/\varepsilon))$ iterations to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to0$. We show that for any fixed positive delay, neither NAG nor HB retains $\sqrtκ$-acceleration on strongly convex quadratics when updating every iteration, for any stable constant step size and positive momentum. We introduce delay-resistant accelerated momentum (DREAM), which decouples gradient-query extrapolation from momentum and uses explicit delay-dependent parameters. DREAM attains a linear convergence rate $1-Θ(1/(τ\sqrtκ))$ for all smooth strongly convex objectives as $κ\to\infty$, yielding complexity matching the delayed first-order lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Our proof combines characteristic-polynomial stability analysis on quadratics with an analytic Zames--Falb integral quadratic constraint certificate. We extend DREAM to smooth convex objectives, obtaining near-optimal iteration complexity up to logarithmic factors for sufficiently small target accuracy. Experiments on strongly convex quadratics and regularized logistic regression corroborate DREAM's accelerated condition-number dependence under delay, unlike NAG and HB, and suggest this scaling persists when parameters use a conservative bound on the true delay.

entry.title: Measuring Sudoku Difficulty: Formulation, Propagation and Uniqueness Certification
entry.summary: Finding a Sudoku completion and proving that the completion is unique are different computational tasks. Despite both concerning the same puzzle, their computational effort need not be closely related. In this paper, we investigate how this relationship depends on the mathematical formulation, solver and measure of computational effort. Using 32,000 uniquely solvable puzzles and 64 harder instances, we compare integer programming formulations and CP-SAT. Further, we prove that the raw natural formulation has an extremely weak linear programming relaxation, even with uniqueness exclusions. Computational experiments show that the relationship between completion and certification effort depends on the formulation, puzzle population, solver and effort measure, rather than on the puzzle alone.

entry.title: A switching proximal gradient method for constrained difference-of-convex optimization problems
entry.summary: We study difference-of-convex optimization problems with several composite inequality constraints and develop a majorization-guided switching proximal gradient (MGSPG) method. Specifically, at each feasible outer point, quadratic majorization and linearization yield a strongly convex composite surrogate problem. To solve this surrogate approximately, we employ a switching proximal gradient (SPG) method, which takes a proximal gradient step for the objective when the current point is nearly feasible and for a most violated constraint otherwise. This construction requires neither projection onto the joint surrogate feasible set nor multiplier computation. By establishing a common invariant ball and using an increasing weight argument, we obtain an \(O(τ^{-1})\) inner complexity bound for SPG. Building on this bound, we show that, under boundedness of the feasible level set and a uniform Slater condition for the surrogates, MGSPG finds an \(\varepsilon\)-KKT point in \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) outer iterations and \(O(\varepsilon^{-4})\) selected component proximal gradient updates. Numerical experiments on SCAD-constrained and groupwise-constrained regression problems demonstrate the viability and computational efficiency of our method compared with existing optimization algorithms.

entry.title: Optimal Control of Scalar Diffusions with Finite Action Sets
entry.summary: We study a scalar finite-horizon controlled diffusion with a finite action set. An action may affect the drift, the instantaneous variance, or both, and performance is assessed by a uniformly convex terminal deviation cost. The model represents systems in which decisions are made continuously in time but only finitely many operating settings are available. Under uniform nondegeneracy and an explicit shape condition on the terminal cost, we show that the value function is classical at positive times, establish global positive upper and lower bounds for its second state derivative, and prove that the ratio of its first and second state derivatives is strictly increasing. This ordering implies that each action's optimality region is connected, the active actions occur in monotone order, and adjacent regions are separated by unique switching boundaries. It also yields an exact coefficient-based screen that removes actions that cannot be optimal on any open state region. For smooth continuous-action benchmarks, both the value loss from restricting the action set and the additional loss from rounding the continuous optimal feedback to the nearest available action decrease quadratically with the action-set resolution. Numerical experiments illustrate the resulting action screens, threshold policies, and implementation losses.

entry.title: ROAR: Restricted 2-Opt And Ruin-and-recreate Heuristic for Large and Extreme Scale Traveling Repairman Problem
entry.summary: The Traveling Repairman Problem minimizes cumulative arrival times rather than the total route length, as in the classical Traveling Salesman Problem. The literature contains several legacy metaheuristics for the TRP; however, most are evaluated on small- and medium-scale instances and show limited scalability for large and extreme datasets. GILS-RVND, the current gold standard in metaheuristic algorithms, performs well on small and medium instances but struggles to scale due to the exhaustive neighborhood search in the RVND phase. To address this limitation, we introduce Restricted 2-Opt And Ruin-and-recreate (ROAR), a Large Neighborhood Search-based method that integrates ruin-and-recreate with greedy insertion and a restricted, insertion-anchored 2-opt operator. Computational experiments demonstrate that ROAR produces high-quality solutions for large-scale instances and outperforms existing methods under strict time limits. We further introduce an O(1)-time, O(1)-space algorithm for evaluating 2-opt moves during a contiguous systematic sweep, which, to the best of our knowledge, is unprecedented. Finally, we evaluate ROAR on instances with up to 200,000 nodes, substantially exceeding the largest instances previously reported in the literature (11,849 nodes).

entry.title: A Two-Stage Optimization Framework for Real-World Large-Scale University Course Timetabling Based on Orthogonalized Hierarchical Modeling and Conflict-Driven ALNS Repair
entry.summary: University course timetabling is a large-scale combinatorial optimization problem involving strongly coupled temporal and resource constraints. This paper proposes a two-stage optimization framework for real-world large-scale university course timetabling, integrating orthogonalized hierarchical modeling with conflict-driven adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) repair. The first stage performs global course-level optimization, while the second identifies residual conflicts through a conflict graph and localizes them into connected conflict regions. The Course--Occurrence--Session representation provides the structural basis for multi-granularity repair, which employs Cluster-, Course-, Occurrence-, and Session-level destroy operators within the ALNS framework, followed by fine-grained greedy repair. The framework is evaluated on a real-world university timetabling instance involving 3,073 course groups, 8,015 scheduling events, 998 student classes, and 1,511 instructors. Ablation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of hierarchical repair granularity and adaptive operator selection. Across ten independent runs, the ALNS + Greedy framework achieves a mean residual conflict count of 18.50, compared with 172 for deterministic Greedy-only repair under the same initial scheduling conditions, representing an 89.24\% reduction. These results support the effectiveness of the proposed conflict-driven hierarchical repair framework for large-scale university course timetabling.

entry.title: Observer-Based Event-Triggered Control of Infinite-Dimensional Linear Systems
entry.summary: We investigate observer-based event-triggered stabilization of infinite-dimensional linear systems, such as those governed by partial differential equations. A Luenberger observer and a feedback gain are assumed to stabilize the closed loop in continuous time, and we study what happens when the control input is only updated at instants generated by a dynamic event-triggering mechanism. Unlike approaches that rely on state-dependent triggering rules, our condition only involves the observer state and the measured output, which makes it implementable when the full state is not measured. It compares the deviation of a monitored signal of the observer since the last update with a threshold made of two parts. The first one is a relative part, proportional to the current size of this signal, and the second one is a positive internal variable, which does not depend on the observer state. In particular, the case where the threshold reduces to the internal variable alone is covered. Under suitable assumptions, we establish the well-posedness of the closed-loop system and the absence of Zeno behavior for general choices of these two parts, and we prove its exponential stability under a small-gain condition on the relative part. We further analyse the existence of a dwell-time, namely a positive lower bound on the time elapsed between two consecutive triggering instants. When the sampled dynamics is bounded, as in finite-dimensional systems or systems with a finite-dimensional unstable part, we obtain a dwell-time independent of the initial data, together with exponential stability. For unbounded generators, we exhibit a system satisfying all our assumptions for which no triggering rule can achieve both a dwell-time independent of the initial data and bounded trajectories.

entry.title: Robust global supply chain reconfiguration under tariff and geopolitical uncertainty
entry.summary: Global supply chains are increasingly exposed to trade policy shocks and physical disruptions arising from common geopolitical events. We develop a robust optimization framework with two decision stages for strategic supply chain reconfiguration. Supplier qualification and transportation arc activation decisions are made before uncertainty is realized, while operational flows adapt afterward. Geopolitical uncertainty is represented through country level shocks that can jointly trigger tariff escalation, policy induced restrictions on cross border capacity, facility disruptions, and physical transportation failures. The resulting min max min problem is reformulated by dualizing the operational recourse problem, yielding a nonconvex mixed integer bilinear adversarial problem solved within a column and constraint generation procedure. Comparison with complete enumeration verifies the implementation on small instances, while experiments on 60 synthetic supply chain networks of varying sizes assess computational performance. The results show that omitting geopolitical transmission channels during strategic design can lead to substantial deterioration in cost and service under full geopolitical stress. Broader protection is achieved primarily through changes in transportation network configuration rather than increased supplier qualification. Robust performance also depends on the severity and composition of geopolitical consequences, with restrictions on cross border capacity exerting a stronger effect than comparable proportional changes in tariff severity over the tested ranges. A geographically grounded case analysis further shows that the value of individual uncertainty channels depends on network structure and geographic exposure.

entry.title: On the Minimum Speed for a Fire Blocking Problem
entry.summary: We consider a dynamic blocking problem: a fire, starting on a bounded open set $R_0\subset\mathbb R^2$, propagates in the plane with unit speed in all directions. To block it, a barrier can be constructed in real time, at speed $λ>0$. A long standing conjecture by the first author states that the fire can be entirely surrounded by the barrier, in finite time, if and only if $λ>2$. The present paper improves on earlier lower bounds. Namely, if $λ\leq Λ=1.62621170228\ldots $ we show that the fire cannot be blocked. We also prove that, if $λ\leq 2$, the fire cannot be blocked by constructing a barrier which is a simple closed curve. More precisely, if the barrier does not contain purely delaying arcs, i.e.~arcs which are eventually surrounded by the fire on both sides, then for $λ<2$ the region burned by the fire at time $t>0$ has area $A(t)>(2-λ)t^2/4$.

entry.title: RoRo stowage planning: a systematic study of mathematical formulations
entry.summary: Stowage planning for Roll-On/Roll-Off (RoRo) vessels can be represented with different mathematical formulations for efficient stowage plans: hybrid-slot, grid-based, and lane-based representations. In this work, we implement and compare three formulations equally across a diverse set of instances. We extend these three representations to handle heterogeneous cargo in terms of size and weight, and to address advanced stability requirements, such as centre of gravity limits, stress force limits, and ballast-water adjustments. We evaluate the models in three configurations: cargo placement, simple stability with centres of gravity limits and ballast adjustments, and full stability, which adds shear-force and bending-moment limits. The tests are conducted on three different vessel sizes and solved with a mixed-integer programming solver. The hybrid-slot and grid-based models both perform well finding solutions for 447 out of 486 instances across all configurations; however, the hybrid-slot model placed 8% more cargo than the grid model. By contrast, the lane model only finds solutions for 142 instances and placed 15% less cargo than the grid-based model. The solutions generated by the hybrid-slot model are validated using a commercial vessel-stability software to verify our stability estimations, showing issues in only 24 of 162 instances, which are easily avoided by tightening the stability constraints. Finally, we address the placement of hazardous and refrigerated cargo in an efficient manner for the hybrid-slot model by employing lazy constraints which is shown to solve realistic sized instances.

entry.title: Verifying Control Invariance of H-Polytopes is coNP-Complete
entry.summary: We prove that verifying whether an H-polytope is control invariant for a discrete-time linear system with polytopic input constraints is \textsc{coNP}-complete. This establishes a fundamental computational complexity barrier for set-theoretic control. As an immediate consequence, the exact computation of maximal control invariant subsets of H-polytopes is \textsc{coNP}-hard. These hardness results hold regardless of whether the input constraint set is given in H- or V-representation.

entry.title: Frequency-Uniform Log-Regret Reinforcement Learning for Diffusions
entry.summary: High-frequency control problems are often studied through time discretization, but refining the timestep $δ$ increases the discrete horizon $H=T/δ$ and can make standard finite-horizon regret guarantees deteriorate even when the physical horizon $T$ is fixed. We study episodic value-based reinforcement learning for Euler discretizations of controlled diffusions. The performance is measured as the cumulative regret over $K$ episodes relative to the optimal policy of the corresponding Euler model. Under stability and regularity conditions on value function gradients, Bellman residual derivatives, and fitted critics, we prove an $\mathcal{O}(\log K)$ regret bound with constants uniform in $δ$. For dynamics with drift linear in unknown parameters and unknown constant diffusion covariance, we verify localized versions of these conditions for a constrained, model-based controlled-diffusion fitted-$Q$ algorithm (CD-FQ) and obtain high-probability $\mathcal{O}(\log K\log\log K)$ regret for fixed and finite $T$, again with constants uniform in $δ$.

entry.title: Robust Log-Contrast Regression for High-Dimensional Compositional Microbiome Data with Outliers
entry.summary: It is well known that microbiome sequencing data are naturally compositional and often have a complex subcomposition structure, as well as a lot of noise and some outliers. These characteristics make classical log-contrast regression difficult to apply, because it is sensitive to extreme values and cannot fully meet the linear constraints of compositional predictors. To tackle these issues, in this paper, we propose a robust log-contrast regression framework that incorporates the Huber loss function along with a Lasso penalty, which not only boosts resistance to outliers but also facilitates sparse variable selection. It is important to note that the general linear constraints, which are explicitly imposed, serve to preserve the algebraic coherence of compositional and subcompositional covariates. Under some mild assumptions, we theoretically prove that the proposed method achieves non-asymptotic guarantees in finite samples, comparable to those of Huber loss estimators, ensuring robustness. To implement the method efficiently, we develop a symmetric Gauss--Seidel-based alternating direction method of multipliers based on its dual formulation with a convergence guarantee, and it is also easy to implement in the sense that each subproblem admits a closed-form solution. To evaluate the statistical performance of the proposed method, we conduct a series of numerical experiments using simulated data and gut microbiome data, which show that the proposed method achieves better estimation accuracy, competitive prediction performance, and more reliable outlier identification than the benchmark method RobRegCC.

entry.title: Error analysis and optimal sample allocation for randomized unbiased estimation: the single term estimator
entry.summary: Randomized unbiased estimation can be highly efficient for approximating expectations of functionals of stochastic differential equations. However, in practice, the optimal computational efficiency is rarely attained due to errors arising from parameter estimation and truncation. The effects of these errors on computational efficiency have not been investigated. In this article, we study the error analysis and optimal sample allocation for the single term estimator. Specifically, under mild assumptions on the estimated parameters, we develop a unified error analysis that incorporates both sources of error, and establish the relevant convergence rates for the computational efficiency loss. Based on this analysis, we further investigate the optimal allocation of the computational budget for parameter estimation, and propose several efficient sample allocation strategies. Numerical experiments support the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods.

entry.title: On the Pontryagin Maximum Principle for Rough Stochastic Differential Equations
entry.summary: We establish first- and second-order Pontryagin (a.k.a. stochastic) maximum principles for rough stochastic control problems with general nonlinear $\mathrm{Lip}^γ$-rough vector fields. This complements the dynamic programming approach of Friz-Lê-Zhang [FLZ26b], and extends the maximum principle of Horst-Zhang [HZ26] beyond affine rough vector fields. The paper concludes with applications to pathwise stochastic optimal control.

entry.title: Axiomatic Learning and Probabilistic Structures with first applications to variants of Arithmetic Machine Learning and beyond
entry.summary: We introduce the Axiomatic Learning Structures (ALS) and Axiomatic Probabilistic Structure (APS) in order to study the interactions of Machine Learning, Optimization, with research frameworks- which, we take the view, can be characterized at the core by the corresponding axioms. The ALS explores the interplays between structures that one is interested in Learning Theory such as Loss functions and the axioms of the objects and transformations involved in these functions. The APS studies the interaction between structures of interest in Probability Theory such as Gibbs distributions, equations with noise, etc. and the axioms of the corresponding objects and transformations. We also introduce in Section 6 Transformations-Axiomatic Based Learning (TABLe) on Mathematical data-sets. One feature of this approach is the ranking of transformations from a table for a certain task based on scores which reflect which transformations work better than others, similarly to when human investigators try various methods on a task. We also study structure recovery from noisy data. In particular, to exemplify the ideas, we consider loss functions which contain derivations and derivations-like transformations. As a first application we study recovery in the context of polynomials with integer coefficients using standard derivatives along with other types of derivations which appear in Arithmetic: the p-derivations which satisfy \textit{different axioms} from the usual derivatives. As a first application of the APS we study a class of noisy (partial/mixed) derivations equations. In the last sections, to provide further potential applications of this framework, we give an overview of an initial simplified Opinion Dynamics model and its (simultaneous) study of rules of updates.

entry.title: Wasserstein approximation of measures via orthogonal frames: statistical and computational complexities
entry.summary: Dimension-reduction methods such as PCA identify a subspace capturing most of the variation in the data, but not a distinguished basis within it. Selecting a basis in which the samples are sparsely represented is a recurring task in unsupervised learning, addressed by methods in factor analysis, dictionary learning, and subspace clustering. We pose this task as Wasserstein approximation of the data distribution by measures supported on the axes of an orthogonal frame, which, in turn, reduces to a nonsmooth optimization problem over the orthogonal group $\mathrm{O}(d)$. We show that, under mild assumptions, both empirical risk minimizers and a locally initialized stochastic gradient method recover the population-optimal frame at the near-parametric rate $\widetilde{O}_d(n^{-1/2})$, where $n$ is the sample size. The main difficulty is that, although the population objective is smooth, the empirical objective is not-this mismatch precludes standard covering arguments. We overcome this issue by replacing Lipschitz continuity of the empirical gradient with a coarsely Lipschitz bound, a tool that may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments support our theoretical findings.

entry.title: QESChunker: A Single Objective Unifies Overlapping and Non-Overlapping Chunking for RAG
entry.summary: Chunking is a fundamental preprocessing step in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), yet most existing chunkers rely primarily on heuristics. We introduce the Question--Evidence-Supervised Chunker (QESChunker), to our knowledge the first method for constructing static chunk indices from question--evidence supervision. QESChunker constructs document-specific chunk indices by optimizing over human-annotated or LLM-generated question--evidence pairs, without access to held-out test queries. We formulate non-overlapping and overlapping index construction through a unified question--evidence utility-maximization objective, turning chunking into a supervised combinatorial optimization problem. Under the non-overlap constraint, the objective decomposes over chunks and can be optimized exactly in polynomial time by dynamic programming. When overlap is allowed, the objective becomes monotone submodular; exact optimization is NP-hard, but our greedy achieves a $(1-1/\sqrt{e})$-approximation. Across two self-constructed and three public datasets, both variants outperform existing chunking methods in complete-evidence recall in nearly all evaluated settings, under the same overlap regime and a fixed hybrid retriever. These results recast chunking as supervised, budget-aware index construction for evidence retrieval.

entry.title: NextEval: An Agent-Based Solver and Benchmark for Derivative-Free Optimization
entry.summary: Derivative-free optimization (DFO) addresses problems where derivatives are unavailable or costly to obtain. This setting often arises in simulation-based and experimental applications, where evaluating the black-box objective can itself be costly. Thus, it remains a central challenge in DFO to effectively exploit accumulated observations to select informative evaluation points under a limited budget. In this light, we introduce the NextEval solver, an agent-based DFO solver, which integrates the capabilities of a large language model (LLM) to guide the sequential selection of evaluation points. Specifically, we establish a system that combines an LLM agent with a numerical environment. The environment provides tools for analyzing past evaluations and executing numerical methods, while maintaining a shared evaluation history and method-specific state to support continuation across method switches. Using observations and tool feedback, the LLM agent selects tools, configures their parameters, and allocates the evaluation budget, while numerical methods compute and evaluate candidate points. Building on this system, we also introduce NextEval Bench, a benchmark protocol for comparing agent configurations on shared DFO tasks using the same numerical tools under matched evaluation budgets and information constraints. Numerical results on low-dimensional DFO problems demonstrate that the NextEval solver outperforms the state-of-the-art DFO baselines in function-evaluation efficiency.

entry.title: Hybridizing 0/1 Knapsack and Priority-Aware TSP for Vehicle Routing: an Applied Variant of the TSP with Profits
entry.summary: Distribution logistics with capacity constraints and service priorities can be modeled as a variant of the \emph{TSP with Profits} (TSPP), in which not all customers need to be visited and the selection of which customers to serve is part of the problem. This paper proposes an applied variant with two adaptations: (i) a 0/1 Knapsack objective function weighted by client priority squared ($v_i \cdot p_i^2$), and (ii) a priority bias in the Nearest Neighbor heuristic for the TSP, parameterized by $α$. The approach is evaluated on a scenario with 14 customers and a 1,100~kg capacity, complemented by a comparative experimental protocol against the classical greedy heuristic ($v_i/w_i$ ordering) and an integer programming solver. Results on the base scenario show 9 customers served, 96.4\% capacity utilization, and R\$~18,392.60 revenue, with all 5 excluded customers being low-priority. A sensitivity analysis of the priority exponent justifies the quadratic choice. The limitations of the hierarchical decomposition are explicitly discussed.

entry.title: Detailed balance and phase transition in Nash equilibria of mean-field Ising game
entry.summary: We study a finite-state mean-field game with entropic control cost. In the large population limit, we show that its stationary Nash equilibria satisfy the detailed balance condition and their distributions take the Gibbsian form with the value function playing the role of a Hamiltonian. We apply the entropic control cost to a ferromagnetic mean-field Ising game and investigate its stationary and non-stationary Nash equilibria. We find that the stationary Nash equilibria exhibit a second-order phase transition from disordered to ordered equilibria as temperature decreases. A center-manifold reduction yields non-stationary Nash equilibrium near the critical temperature and reveals the critical slowing down in the relaxation toward the stationary Nash equilibrium.

entry.title: Linear Programming Upper Bounds for the Coil-in-the-Box Problem
entry.summary: Let $S_n$ denote the maximum length of a coil in the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$, i.e., a simple cycle whose induced subgraph has no additional chords. We combine classical square-counting identities and structural properties of maximum coils with new valid combinatorial inequalities into a parameterized linear program whose optimal value provides an upper bound for $S_n$. For $n\ge13$, we construct two analytic dual feasible solutions. Their objective values yield upper bounds on $S_n$, and the smaller value is the exact optimum of the parameterized LP. One dual solution results in the bound \[ S_n\le 2^{n-1} \frac{8n(n-1)(5n-14)} {40n^3-131n^2+4n+136-(5n-14)\lfloor3n/4\rfloor}, \] which improves upon the upper bounds in Lukito, Lukito-van Zanten, and Zémor for $13\le n\le19853$. The second yields the upper bound \[ S_n\le 2^{n-1}\left( 1-\frac1{30\sqrt{3n}}+O(n^{-1}) \right), \] improving upon the asymptotic upper bound of Zémor. Taken together, the two bounds improve upon the upper bounds for $S_n$ in Lukito, Lukito-van Zanten, and Zémor for every $n\ge13$.

entry.title: Shape optimization under minimal width and constant width constraints
entry.summary: In this paper we study shape optimization problems for planar convex sets with prescribed minimal width or constant width. We prove that the Reuleaux triangle minimizes torsional rigidity among sets of constant width. We also show that the first Dirichlet-Laplace eigenvalue is maximized by the equilateral triangle under a minimal width constraint and by the Reuleaux triangle under a constant width constraint. The proofs use subsets consisting of a disk and three straight or circular caps. Reflection arguments reduce the study to equilateral configurations, which contain a polygon or a disk polygon depending on one parameter. The same cap constructions give a common proof of the known area, Cheeger and inner parallel area inequalities, and yield sharp bounds for all positive moments of the distance to the boundary. We also prove sharp inequalities for concentric disk intersections and decreasing radial integrals, and compare interaction energies for kernels close to a positive constant. This includes a nonempty interval of positive Riesz exponents. Finally, we investigate whether inclusion monotonicity and Minkowski concavity suffice to obtain these comparisons for other functionals.

entry.title: Asynchronous Parallel Computation of Lagrangian Bounds for Mixed-Integer Stochastic Programs by Frank-Wolfe Methods within Projective Hedging
entry.summary: We describe an asynchronous parallel method to calculate Lagrangian bounds for mixed-integer stochastic programming problems. As in some prior work, we use a fully corrective Frank-Wolfe method on subproblems within a decomposition method, eventually optimizing subproblems for individual scenarios over the convex hulls of their integer-feasible vertices. However, instead of using progressive hedging as our decomposition algorithm, we employ an asynchronous projective hedging method. Like our earlier work on projective hedging, our algorithm need only solve a subset of the scenario subproblems at each iteration. Here, we further exploit the capabilities of projective hedging to create a parallel implementation capable of fully asynchronous operation. As we demonstrate empirically, this capability can lead to significant efficiency improvements when the subproblems are solved by Frank-Wolfe and have highly variable solve times.

entry.title: Multi-time-scale Control of Power Systems
entry.summary: The power grid has been dominated by large synchronous generators and clearly separated control layers. Today, power-electronics energy conversion interfaces are rapidly being deployed calling for another look at system-level control hierarchies. This article examines how multi-time-scale modeling, feedback control, and feedback optimization can help reinterpret the traditional organically grown hierarchy of primary control, automatic generation control, and economic dispatch, and enable new approaches for control of contemporary power systems. Beginning with an overview of power system models and conventional operational practices, the article develops connections to modern control architectures that can coordinate heterogeneous resources, account for operational constraints, and exploit faster actuation without overlooking first-principles physics.

entry.title: Hidden Convexity in Multi-Retailer Cold-Chain Allocation: A Cholesky-Spectral Second-Order Cone Programming Approach
entry.summary: Several dairy retailers share a refrigerated cold-chain network, each allocating products across heat-sensitivity subgroups to maximize quadratic-fractional efficiency (DEA style). This formulation measures spoilage risk per unit of logistics cost, separating technical from scale efficiency. The single-agent problem is a non-convex fractional QCQP, while the multi-retailer game forms a generalized Nash equilibrium problem (GNEP) with a shared risk-budget constraint, which is generally NP-hard. Governed by the Arrhenius spoilage law, the thermal-risk covariance inherits a rank-one-plus-diagonal structure that unlocks hidden convexity. The authors propose the HSDI (Hidden SOCP Dinkelbach Iteration) algorithm via a joint Cholesky-spectral transform. Key contributions include: 1. Establishing simultaneous diagonalization of without requiring matrix commutativity. 2. Deriving an explicit sufficient condition for exact second-order cone programming (SOCP) relaxation, alongside a closed-form suboptimality bound for inexact regimes. 3. Proving global convergence: the outer Dinkelbach loop converges Q-superlinearly (exact) or R-linearly (inexact), and the coupled variational-equilibrium (VE) iteration converges R-linearly under strong monotonicity, achieving an overall complexity while ensuring Lipschitz stability of the primal-dual pair. Calibrated on Vietnam and US dairy markets, HSDI matches the objective value of multi-start non-linear baselines without random restarts, yielding global optima under exactness. HSDI exhibits an empirical scaling exponent of 0.93 (versus 1.30 for SLSQP), offering a certified polynomial-time framework and a stable shadow price for prioritizing cold-chain investments.

entry.title: Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control via Trajectory Optimization
entry.summary: The curse of dimensionality associated with solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for the value function remains a key obstacle for real-time optimal feedback control of high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems. This is especially severe in aerospace applications such as relaminarizing unsteady turbulent flows and recovering from aerodynamic stall where nonlinear dynamics play a significant role. We introduce Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control (BASOC), a model reduction framework which seeks to find directions in state space along which the value function is most sensitive, and the distribution of states exhibits maximum variance along optimal trajectories. BASOC leverages trajectory optimization and the Pontryagin minimum principle to obtain state and co-state (value function gradient) data along locally optimal trajectories for constructing state and gradient covariance matrices. Balancing these matrices provides an oblique projection for approximating the value function, which can also be used to construct reduced-order models and surrogate feedback control laws. We show that for linear-quadratic optimal control problems, BASOC becomes equivalent to a snapshot method for initial condition balancing of the optimally controlled closed-loop realization. The framework is demonstrated on a nonlinear three-dimensional system where POD and balanced truncation are known to perform poorly, and on the nonlinear complex Ginzburg-Landau equation to demonstrate feasibility for larger-scale systems.

entry.title: AHEAD: Adaptive Neural Acceleration for Large-Scale Linear Programming
entry.summary: Large-scale linear programs with millions of variables and constraints strain time and memory budgets. First-order methods such as the primal-dual hybrid gradient scale to this regime because they avoid matrix factorizations, but they require many iterations. Learned accelerators can reduce these iterations, yet fewer iterations do not guarantee a shorter solve. Learning inference also takes time, and running the accelerator longer trades solver time for inference time. Existing unrolled accelerators handle this trade-off poorly: each layer processes every variable and constraint, the predicted iterates still need solver refinement, and every instance runs the same layers. We therefore ask: What neural accelerator design achieves end-to-end speedups on large-scale linear programs across sizes and target accuracies? We introduce AHEAD, an accelerator that predicts step sizes for first-order linear programming solvers while keeping their update rules. Its weight-shared predictor reads compact solver statistics and rescales the primal and dual step sizes, so each warm-start iteration stays inexpensive and a short warm-start phase hands the solver a warm start. A learned handoff policy sets the number of warm-start iterations for each instance and target accuracy, after which the solver finishes under its own termination criterion. On packing linear programs with up to $10^7$ variables, AHEAD achieves $6.5$--$11.6\times$ end-to-end speedups over Gurobi's first-order solver from a cold start, including on instances of unseen sizes and distributions. The gains extend to PageRank linear programs and hold across difficulty levels and target accuracies.

entry.title: A unified family of multiblock ADMM schemes by means of graph splitting
entry.summary: This paper introduces a novel unified family of multiblock ADMM schemes by combining Gabay duality with a graph-based splitting methodology. This framework allows us to recover existing ADMM algorithms as particular instances, as well as to generate new ones by varying the underlying network topology. We focus specifically on the case of the complete graph, a structure of significant practical interest due to its dense connectivity, for which we provide a fully explicit and directly implementable scheme. We further derive an equivalent reformulation of the proposed family in which the algorithm is expressed in terms of a reduced set of dual variables, which clarifies its connection to the classical ADMM framework. Numerical experiments are conducted to compare the performance of different graph choices, showing particularly favorable results for the complete graph.

entry.title: Proximal Point Newton Methods for Nonconvex Optimization
entry.summary: Tensor methods offer improved complexity guarantees for nonconvex optimization, but evaluating high-order derivatives and solving the corresponding subproblems can be computationally expensive. In this paper, we develop a proximal point Newton framework that exploits third-derivative smoothness using only gradients and Hessians. Under Hessian Lipschitz continuity, a single-loop proximal point Newton method that alternates between negative-curvature directions and Newton steps finds an $(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H)$-approximate second-order stationary point within $\mathcal{O}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-3/2},\varepsilon_H^{-3}\})$ second-order oracle evaluations. When the third derivative is also Lipschitz continuous, we introduce an accelerated proximal point Newton method and obtain a dimension-free complexity of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-4/3},\varepsilon_H^{-2}\})$, matching that of the third-order tensor methods up to logarithmic factors without constructing tensors or solving tensor subproblems. We further develop an adaptive inexact Newton--CG variant that requires no prior knowledge of Lipschitz constants and preserves the improved oracle complexity with high probability. Under uniformly bounded queried Hessians, this variant achieves a Hessian-vector product complexity of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-5/3},\varepsilon_H^{-5/2}\})$, improving upon the previous $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-3}\varepsilon_H^{5/2},\varepsilon_H^{-7/2}\})$ result attained by existing second-order methods such as cubic regularized Newton method and Newton--CG method. Preliminary numerical experiments are encouraging.

entry.title: Cost benefits of designing carbon capture processes for part-load operation of power plants
entry.summary: As fossil power plants increasingly cycle to balance variable renewable generation, carbon capture plants must be designed for a wide range of part-load operating conditions, to avoid excessive capital costs. However, accounting for the variability in design optimization yields higher computational complexity, and is therefore not a current design methodology. Here, we apply two-stage stochastic optimization to identify optimal carbon capture plant designs accounting for part-load flue gas conditions. We reduce computational complexity through a data-driven approach-to-equilibrium model of the absorption and desorption processes. Operating scenarios are derived from real-world part-load operation data of coal and natural gas combined cycle power plants. Our results demonstrate that designs optimized over multiple operating scenarios substantially reduce equipment sizes, lowering capital costs by 5-9 % at the expense of higher operating costs, resulting in a moderate reduction in total annualized cost by 0.5-1.6 %. The lowest costs are achieved when targeting an average capture target across operating scenarios, which allows CO2 capture to be shifted from full-load to part-load periods to reduce peak equipment sizes without compromising overall CO2 emission reductions. These cost benefits are robust across sensitivity analyses and increase with higher shares of part-load operation. Thus, part-load variability should be considered at the design stage, particularly for plants subject to variable load.

entry.title: Stability of Doubly Indexed Discrete Linear Systems
entry.summary: We study the stability of the two-dimensional discrete dynamical system defined by \[ x_{i,j} = A x_{i-1,j} + B x_{i,j-1},\] where $A, B \in \mathcal{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$. Although this system, commonly known as the Fornasini-Marchesini model, has been examined for decades, several key stability results have lacked rigorous proofs. This paper establishes precise and self-contained criteria for Lyapunov, asymptotic, and neutral stability under general bounded boundary conditions. In particular, we prove that asymptotic stability is equivalent to the spectral condition $ ρ(z_1 A + z_2 B) < 1 $ for all $ |z_1| \leq 1, |z_2| \leq 1 $. We further analyze the commutative case, derive recurrence relations for anti-diagonal sums, and present new examples and counterexamples illustrating the nuances of stability. The results are complemented by sufficient conditions based on matrix norms, Lyapunov functions, and the joint spectral radius.

entry.title: Minimax-Optimal Small-Loss Bounds for Online Linear Optimisation on $\ell_p$ Balls
entry.summary: We study full-information online linear optimisation on the unit $\ell_p$ ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$, for fixed $2\le p<\infty$ and losses of dual norm at most one. Let $Δ_T$ denote the cumulative loss of the best fixed action above each round's minimum. A follow-the-regularised-leader (FTRL) algorithm attains, on every loss sequence and without knowing $T$ or $Δ_T$, regret $O_p(1+\min\{Δ_T^{1-1/p},\, d^{1/2-1/p}\sqrt{Δ_T}\})$. Matching lower bounds show that this rate is minimax for each fixed $p$, and its constant $(2+o(1))p/\log p$ is optimal as $p\to\infty$ among guarantees uniform in $d$ and $T$. The algorithm uses a bounded radial regulariser and switches at most once to its quadratic augmentation. On some paths where follow-the-leader (FTL) has regret one, its regret grows with $T$. A switching extension keeps the sharp constant and also guarantees $\mathrm{Reg}_T\le 2\,\mathrm{Reg}_T^{\mathrm{FTL}}$. For i.i.d. losses whose mean has no zero coordinates, we compute the exact $\log T$ coefficient of the expected regret, which separates FTL's variance term from the bias of the regulariser.

entry.title: Optimal tradeoffs between variance and sensitivity, via Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry
entry.summary: While the goal of classical statistical theory is to minimize the variance of unbiased estimators, an additional goal of some recent research is to minimize or constrain other notions of the instability of estimators. In particular, a subset of the authors recently introduced a notion of instability termed "sensitivity", which represents the expected amount that an estimator would change if its inputs were infinitesimally perturbed. In this work, we study the multiobjective problem of minimizing both the variance and sensitivity over unbiased estimators in a given statistical model, and we aim to determine Pareto optimal tradeoffs between these two objectives. Our main results show that the Pareto front for these tradeoffs is precisely determined by endowing the statistical model with the Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry, which interpolates between the Hellinger and Wasserstein geometries that are known to be associated, respectively, with the separate minimization of variance and sensitivity. We also develop a $Z$-estimation technique which constructs estimators that asymptotically achieve Pareto optimal pairs of variance and sensitivity. While computing the Pareto front and constructing the resulting estimators in practice requires solving a continuum of partial differential equations, we fully execute this program in some parametric examples of interest where the analysis is already non-trivial. Our results also shed light on some classical statistical problems, for example by showing that the maximum likelihood estimator achieves the smallest asymptotic sensitivity among all estimators achieving the optimal asymptotic variance.

entry.title: Data-Driven Stochastic Control of Delayed Air-Conditioning Systems
entry.summary: We consider a stochastic optimal control problem arising in the operation of industrial air-conditioning systems with delayed activation effects. The delayed transition between inactive and operational regimes induces a non-Markovian structure in the controlled dynamics. We derive a regression-based discrete dynamic programming algorithm on nested state-control grids. We give a probabilistic proof of convergence of the idealized time-discrete dynamic programming problem to the continuous-time value function. Numerical experiments based on calibrated multidimensional forecast-tracking Ornstein--Uhlenbeck models illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

entry.title: A Stochastic Proximal-Gradient Method for Regularized Generally Constrained Continuous Optimization
entry.summary: A stochastic proximal-gradient method is proposed and analyzed for solving regularized optimization problems subject to nonlinear equality constraints and nonnegativity bounds. The objective function's values and gradients are available only through inexact stochastic oracles. The method decomposes each trial step into one component that reduces linearized infeasibility and a second component that seeks optimality while preserving that reduction. Trial steps are accepted or rejected through a relaxed sufficient decrease condition subject to stochastic merit function evaluations. Without assuming unbiasedness of stochastic gradient estimates, it is proved under reasonable assumptions that the method reaches an $ε$-KKT point within $O(ε^{-2})$ iterations with high probability. This guarantee further implies almost-sure termination in finitely many iterations and an $O(ε^{-2})$ bound on the expected iteration complexity.

entry.title: Learning Behavioral Parameters of Network Equilibrium Models from Aggregate Mobility Data
entry.summary: Estimating travel behavior parameters is essential for understanding current travel patterns and for forecasting how travelers may respond to future changes in transportation systems. However, reliable estimation remains difficult when behavior must be inferred from sparse and aggregate observations, especially when jointly recovering several behavioral components. In this paper, we develop a bi-level estimation program for a combined destination, mode and route choice model with congestion. The inner level is a convex program at given scale parameters, and returns the taste coefficients as its dual variables together with the equilibrium travel pattern. The outer level selects the scale parameters by out-of-sample prediction, measured by how well the modeled travel pattern predicts observations withheld from estimation. To solve the bi-level problem at scale, we propose a matrix-free Hierarchical Lagrangian Dual algorithm as the inner solver and an outer search by implicit differentiation, which uses the sensitivities of the inner solution to enable efficient search over the scale parameters and reaches the calibrated scales in a handful of iterations. We validate the approach on Los Angeles County using public origin-destination, mode-share and traffic-count data. Our approach scales to a county-level problem with 2.7 million variables and substantially improves computational efficiency over a general-purpose conic solver. Compared with the fixed-scale benchmark, the calibrated model improves predictive performance at the destination and mode levels, with consistent gains across complementary goodness-of-fit measures.

entry.title: Computing Data-Aware Diagonal Frame Decompositions
entry.summary: We present a method for computing a specific type of matrix decomposition that combines a structured framework with data-driven adaptation. This framework allows for an efficient and stable representation of signals or images using frames by identifying sets of vectors that naturally capture the essential features of the given data. The resulting decomposition enables the development of regularization techniques that enhance the quality of reconstruction by preserving important signal characteristics while suppressing noise. We develop an optimization-based algorithm to compute the decomposition and establish convergence properties of the resulting iterates. Numerical experiments on synthetic data and tomographic image reconstruction illustrate the behavior of the proposed method and its performance compared to conventional spectral regularization methods.

entry.title: Supply Chain Information Sharing among Competitors: Profit-Based Participation under Market Shocks
entry.summary: Sharing information can help coordinate supply chain decisions in response to market shocks. Yet, firms must weigh these benefits against the risk of strengthening competitors. We study when competing firms voluntarily join an information-sharing platform to exchange information about market shocks while retaining operational autonomy. Firms differ in information capabilities and decide whether to participate before private signals are realized, creating stochastic information asymmetry. We model participation and quantity decisions as a two-stage dynamic game with incomplete information. For two horizontal competitors, we derive closed-form equilibrium participation strategies that reveal how information power and production efficiency shape participation. Numerical analysis examines more complex supply chain networks. We find that supply chain characteristics impact participation and the level of information asymmetry is a key factor in the equilibrium platform profiles. Firms with similar information power may benefit from joining forces to reduce their competitive disadvantage against higher information power competitors. Cost-inefficient firms may be less willing to participate because their competitors can exploit shared information, and uncertainty can serve as a competitive shield by restricting the actions of more efficient competitors. However, when several competitors join the platform, a cost-inefficient firm may also choose to participate to avoid an informational disadvantage.

entry.title: SCAFFOLD under Hessian Similarity: Sharp Convergence Rates
entry.summary: One of the main challenges of federated learning is heterogeneous data split among the clients, leading to biased local updates called client drift. The SCAFFOLD algorithm (Karimireddy et al., 2020) corrects client drift with control variates, but its relation to the similarity of client data is not yet fully understood: the original similarity-based guarantees cover only quadratics with a stronger second-order similarity assumption, and a follow-up weakly convex analysis (Luo et al., 2025) obtains a $\sqrt{Lδ}$ dependence for $L$-smooth losses with averaged Hessian similarity $δ$. We analyze SCAFFOLD with minibatch-based control variates and establish linear dependence on Hessian similarity beyond quadratics, for both convex and nonconvex objectives. In particular, for convex objectives with exact gradients, $R$ SCAFFOLD rounds with $K$ local steps lead to an objective gap of order $(L/K+δ)D_0^2/R$, where $D_0$ is the initial distance to a minimizer. When $K=Θ(L/δ)$, it improves the minibatch SGD rate by a factor $Θ(L/δ)$. For nonconvex objectives, we prove an analogous stationarity guarantee under uniform Hessian similarity for a client-selection variant. In both settings, we extend these guarantees to stochastic gradients and prove matching lower bounds for the analyzed methods with constant local stepsizes. We also show that, under partial participation, even identical clients need not obtain the full communication benefit of additional local steps.

entry.title: Efficient ADMM for Soft-Constrained Quadratic Programs via Generalized Slack Projections
entry.summary: Quadratic programs (QPs) are a core building block in many applications. In practice, constraints are often softened with slack variables to guarantee feasibility. The standard approach tackles this by introducing additional decision variables, growing the resulting optimization problem. In this paper, we propose an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) scheme for a broad class of convex slack penalty functions, including all $\ell_k$-norms, without increasing the problem size. The only change to the ADMM scheme is a modified slack projection function, while the remaining algorithm stays the same. We demonstrate our approach on numerical examples, showing significant speedups, and show its flexibility on an energy optimization problem.

entry.title: ADACT: PDE-Constrained Thermal Hardware/Software Co-Design Adjoint-Driven Optimal Control via Finite Difference Discretization
entry.summary: By virtue of the sheer compute demands of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC), modern multi-core microprocessors suffer from severe power density limits and thermal throttling, entailing an urgent need for principled methods for predictive, physics-informed dynamical thermal management (DTM). Here, we introduce a hardware/software co-design physics-informed PDE-constrained DTM throttling optimal control algorithm, ADACT (Adjoint-Driven Adaptive Co-Design Thermal Control), that minimizes thermal risk and cooling energy overhead while maximizing core execution throughput. The underlying physical temperature field is governed by a two-dimensional nonhomogeneous parabolic reaction-diffusion equation with spatially localized, time-varying power source terms and variable convective cooling subject to nonhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. We employ a discretization of the continuous state PDE via a Crank-Nicolson finite difference scheme with a 5-point discrete Laplacian operator on a uniform spatial mesh, which preserves unconditional numerical stability and $O(Δx^2 + Δy^2 + Δt^2)$ second-order temporal and spatial accuracy. To efficiently compute exact gradients, we construct and implement a continuous backward-in-time adjoint state method with L-BFGS as our optimization algorithm of choice. The accuracy and second-order convergence rates of both forward state and backward adjoint solvers are quantitatively verified via the Method of Manufactured Solutions (MMS), and gradient accuracy is validated using directional derivative Taylor tests. Numerical experiments demonstrate that ADACT dynamically throttles software power workloads and modulates hardware cooling efforts to strictly uphold physical thermal thresholds while maintaining operational throughput.

entry.title: Local Algebraic Stability of Wasserstein Gradient Descent-Ascent and Mean Field Langevin Dynamics without Spectral Gap
entry.summary: We study the local stability of Wasserstein gradient descent-ascent (GDA) for entropy regularized two-player zero-sum games on noncompact domains. When one or both equilibrium measures fail to satisfy a Poincaré inequality, the spectral gap arguments underlying local exponential convergence are unavailable. we show that Wasserstein GDA converges algebraically to the mixed Nash equilibrium in chi-squared divergence, provided the initial relative density is a small perturbation in $L^2$ with bounded algebraic moments. The proof has two main ingredients: a cancellation in a negative Sobolev energy estimate, and a bootstrap argument that keeps the moments bounded uniformly in time. For polynomial-tailed equilibria, we construct perturbations supported far out in the tails that survive over diffusive time scales, which gives algebraic lower bounds on the worst-case relaxation rate. We also establish analogous local algebraic stability and lower bound results for mean-field Langevin dynamics, when the equilibrium fails to satisfy a spectral gap.

entry.title: Constraint Learning by Optimizing over Trained Neural Networks: A Pragmatic Tutorial
entry.summary: Constraint learning is an emerging paradigm of modeling optimization problems with the help of machine learning. In this paradigm, trained machine learning models are embedded into the optimization model. For example, we can learn constraints empirically from available data, or we can avoid using a nonlinear objective function by learning a simpler approximation for it. Neural networks become a compelling option if the machine learning models must capture more elaborate and nuanced relationships. However, optimization models embedding neural networks may become too large or too slow to solve. In this tutorial, we present practical considerations for an effective and efficient use of constraint learning with neural networks and validate it with a case study highlighting the benefit of smaller and sparser networks.

entry.title: Benchmarking quantum-annealing-based approaches for factory layout planning
entry.summary: The earlystage of factory layout planning has a direct effect on the operating costs, efficiency, and productivity of manufacturing systems. Conventional automated planning approaches often face a trade-off between solution quality and computational effort. Recent studies have investigated the potential of quantum annealing (QA) for solving factory layout planning problems. However, existing studies have mainly focused on individual QA-based formulations, whereas current hybrid QA solvers support multiple model types that combine QA and classical methods. To explore the potential of QA for factory layout planning, this paper benchmarks four QA based approaches implemented with the corresponding solvers, including an iterative binary quadratic model (IBQM), a hybrid discrete quadratic model (HDQM), a hybrid constrained quadratic model (HCQM), and a hybrid nonlinear model (HNLM). To improve scalability, an iterative decomposition strategy is developed for IBQM, while a candidate selection procedure is introduced for HDQM. The approaches are benchmarked against genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization, and a hybrid tabu search and simulated annealing approach on 14 layout instances with different layout sizes, geometric complexity, spatial restrictions, and transport route configurations. The comparative analysis considers solution quality, computation time, and scalability. The results show that QA-based approaches achieve competitive solution quality and substantial computational advantages, reducing computation time by up to 94.51% relative to the classical reference methods. Among them, IBQM obtains the best solution quality in 78.6% of the instances, with a maximum improvement of 17.41% associated with an 81.34% reduction in computation time. These findings provide a basis for their further application in industrial layout planning.

entry.title: Autonomous Structural Discovery Of Bioprocess Dynamics And Kinetics Via LLM-Driven Agents
entry.summary: High-fidelity digital twins in continuous biomanufacturing are often bottlenecked by incomplete kinetic models, while standard data-driven algorithms (e.g., SINDy, PINNs) lack interpretability or impose rigid physical assumptions. This paper introduces a hybrid closed-loop architecture for autonomous kinetic state-space discovery driven by a Large Language Model (LLM) agent. The framework employs a sequential "isolation-peeling" methodology across orthogonal operational regimes. This algorithmic peeling mathematically decouples entangled multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (catalytic) biological rate law. Grounded in a Two-Level Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) library, the framework utilizes Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) and logarithmic decomposition to decouple complex cell growth kinetics into orthogonal multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (regulatory) residual channels. When statistical degeneracy occurs an Active Design of Experiments (DoE) controller dynamically triggers targeted perturbations to decorrelate competing model hypotheses. Evaluated on a continuous stirred-tank reactor exhibiting unmodeled Haldane inhibition, Luong product toxicity, and secondary metabolite autocatalysis, the framework autonomously expanded the state space and recovered ground-truth parameters with under 6% error without a priori kinetic knowledge.

entry.title: Square-Root Clustered Lasso for High-Dimensional Linear Regression with Finite-Sample Theory and Efficient Algorithm Implementation
entry.summary: This paper proposes a square-root clustered Lasso penalized method for high-dimensional linear regression. By integrating square-root loss with the clustered Lasso penalty, the resulting method enables flexible regression modeling and allows tuning parameter selection independent of the unknown noise level. We establish weak decomposability of the clustered Lasso penalty and a noise-level-free tuning strategy under Gaussian noise. Furthermore, we establish the finite-sample prediction accuracy guarantees for the proposed method. The inherent nonsmoothness of the square-root loss and clustered Lasso penalty poses considerable computational difficulties. To resolve this issue, we develop an efficient semismooth Newton-based proximal augmented Lagrangian algorithm (N-ALM) to solve the corresponding dual optimization problem. The subproblems arising in the iteration are efficiently tackled by the semismooth Newton method, which fully utilizes the sparsity structure of the generalized Jacobian. We further establish global convergence and a local linear rate for the distance to the KKT solution set under suitable conditions; the local rate becomes superlinear when the penalty parameter tends to infinity. We conduct numerical experiments on real-world datasets to evaluate the computational performance of N-ALM. The results demonstrate that N-ALM solves the tested high-dimensional SRCL problems accurately and substantially reduces running times compared with d-ADMM.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Assortment Optimization and Matching under MNL Choice
entry.summary: We develop a unified framework for assortment optimization and matching under multinomial logit (MNL) choice, yielding simple algorithms and analyses across a broad class of problems. The framework centers on a single-customer assortment problem in which the firm commits to eligible products before their independent availabilities are revealed. A simple threshold policy achieves a tight $1/2$ guarantee against a benchmark that selects its assortment after observing availability and may control dependence subject to the same marginal probability bounds. This guarantee accommodates cardinality constraints and adversarial removal of excess available products. Combined with problem-specific linear programming relaxations, the framework yields $1/2$ guarantees for standard two-sided assortment optimization, customization under mixtures of MNL models, ride-hailing notifications, multi-round broadcast matching, and MNL prophet inequalities, and a $1/4$ guarantee for fully static two-sided assortment optimization. Across these applications, we improve approximation factors, extend guarantees to more general revenues and cardinality constraints, and retain existing factors against stronger benchmarks.

entry.title: Initialization Stability and Convergence of Projected Langevin Dynamics
entry.summary: The entropic regularized optimal transport (EOT) plays a fundamental role in the computation of optimal transport. In \cite{CLP}, the authors proposed a gradient flow approach to EOT, and derived a projected Langevin diffusion that converges in distribution to the solution of EOT when initialized with a coupling between the two given marginals. In this paper, motivated by samplings of optimal couplings for EOT, we analyze the projected Langevin dynamics with arbitrary initial distribution, and prove that its long time behavior is the same as if it was initialized from a coupling.

entry.title: Quadratic Returns for a Moving Water Tank: An Explicit Right Inverse and a Sylvester Representation
entry.summary: Coron's return method established local nonlinear controllability of a moving water tank in sufficiently large time. We study the quadratic response at uniform equilibrium, where the acceleration input in the linearized model cannot excite the Fourier modes of the fluid with even indices. At three one-way wave crossings (T=3), we construct a nonzero smooth acceleration, whose first two final-state coefficients vanish. A planar curve reduces this cancellation to a scalar identity. At this reference acceleration, two integrations give an explicit control correction that preserves the linear return and produces any given leading change in the quadratic final state. The correction maps periodic $H^r$ targets with zero mean to $H^r$ controls for every nonnegative integer $r$. A contraction argument also gives local exact solvability of the quadratic final-state equation. Finally, a time-dependent Sylvester equation provides an alternative representation of the coupling responsible for the second-order correction. The associated change of state coordinates involves one spatial derivative, while the control correction preserves regularity in appropriate Sobolev spaces. These results concern the first two variation equations and not yet the fully nonlinear model.

entry.title: Accelerated Push-Pull with Local Updates for Decentralized Stochastic Optimization
entry.summary: We consider decentralized stochastic nonconvex optimization over directed networks. Push--Pull provides an efficient decentralized optimization framework for such networks, but in the stochastic setting, gradient variance can slow its convergence and complicate the analysis of linear speedup. Motivated by this observation, we incorporate recursive momentum into stochastic Push--Pull for variance reduction, yielding the accelerated stochastic Push--Pull (ASPP) algorithm. Under mean-squared smoothness, we prove that ASPP improves the convergence rate of stochastic Push--Pull and achieves asymptotic linear speedup with respect to the number of agents. To further reduce communication, we develop LASPP, a local-update variant of ASPP that allows each agent to perform multiple local updates between communication rounds. We show that LASPP achieves an additional asymptotic linear speedup with respect to the number of local steps. With a suitable number of local steps, LASPP reduces communication complexity while maintaining the same stochastic gradient complexity as ASPP. Numerical experiments on real datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

entry.title: Regularization and Full Support for the CBO Equation with Measure Initial Data
entry.summary: We prove global well-posedness and regularization for the isotropic consensus-based optimization equation with initial probability measures of finite fourth moment. Under suitable weight decay assumptions, after any nonconstant consensus motion, both the density and the consensus trajectory become smooth, and all spatial Sobolev norms are locally bounded in time. The proof uses a Fourier commutator estimate, localization and iteration, followed by a nonlinear time bootstrap. Counterexamples show that smoothing can fail at a stationary consensus point. For non-Dirac initial data, we also prove positivity away from the consensus point and full support at every positive time in all dimensions.
